newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Quebrada Blanca says 2-3 weeks stockpiles.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Quebrada Blanca says 2-3 weeks stockpiles.

text.p: Cominco Ltd's Quebrada Blanca copper mine in Chile has stockpiles sufficient to meet two to three weeks' shipments in case workers strike next week, general manager James Drake said Wednesday.
"Obviously we would have in the order of perhaps two to three weeks of deliveries," Drake told Reuters by telephone from Santiago.

Workers at Quebrada Blanca in northern Chile will vote Sunday on whether to accept the company's final wage offer in scheduled negotiations. But even if they do vote to reject the offer, Chilean law forbids any strike to begin for at least three days to allow further negotiations to take place.
Canadian-owned Quebrada Blanca, which has been in wage negotiations since mid-March, produces about 75,000 tonnes of copper in cathodes a year at a mine near the Bolivian border.
The mine's workforce went on strike for a week while negotiating their previous labor contracts two-and-a-half years ago.
About 70 percent of the mine's workforce of 500 people is unionized.
